original_value: Abstract Purpose Compared with traditional course materials used in the classroom, the massive open online course (MOOC) forum that delivers unlimited learning content to students has various advantages. Yet MOOC has also received criticism recently, notably the problem of extremely low participation rates in its discussion forums. This study aims to explore the correlation between forum activity and student course grade in MOOC, and identify more accurately the forum activity levels of participants and the quality of threads in MOOC. Design/Methodology/Approach We crawled students’ tests, final exams, exercises, discussions performance data and total scores from a course in Chinese College MOOC from May 2014 to August 2014. And we use the data to analyze the correlation between Forum Participation and Course Performance based on nonparametric tests as well as multiple linear regressions with the software of R. The study provides definitions and algorithms of super degrees based on the supernetwork model to help find high-quality threads and active participants. Findings A positive correlation between forum activity and course grade is found in this study. Students participate in the forum have better performance than those who do not. Using the definitions and algorithms of super degrees in the supernetwork, forum activity levels of participants as well as the quality of threads they employ are identified. Research limitation Only limited representative forum participants and threads are used to analyze the activity level and significance of the MOOC forum. Also, the study only investigates one Chinese course on information retrieval. More data and more data sources could be helpful in better understanding the MOOC forum phenomenon. Practical implications As super degrees can reveal more latent information and recognize high-quality threads as well as active participants, these parameters can be used to assess needs to improve forum settings and alleviate the problem of low forum participation. The proposed super degrees can be applied in social network domains for further research. Originality/Value Definitions and algorithms of super degrees are provided and used for forum analysis. Super degrees can be applied to find high-quality threads and active participants, which is beneficial to guide students to participate in these high-quality threads and have a better understanding of knowledge MOOC provides.

result.paraphrase: Abstract Purpose Compared with traditional classroom course materials, massive open online courses (MOOCs) offer students unlimited learning content and several advantages. However, MOOCs have recently drawn criticism, especially for extremely low participation in discussion forums. This study seeks to examine the relationship between forum activity and student course grades in MOOCs, and to more accurately identify participants’ forum activity levels and thread quality. Design/Methodology/Approach We collected students’ test, final exam, exercise, discussion performance data, and total scores from a Chinese College MOOC course between May 2014 and August 2014. Using R, we analyzed the relationship between forum participation and course performance with nonparametric tests and multiple linear regression. The study also presents super-degree definitions and algorithms based on the supernetwork model to help identify high-quality threads and active participants. Findings The study finds a positive correlation between forum activity and course grade. Students who participate in the forum perform better than those who do not. With the supernetwork-based super-degree definitions and algorithms, the activity levels of participants and the quality of the threads they use are identified. Research limitation The analysis uses only a limited number of representative forum participants and threads to examine MOOC forum activity and significance. It also focuses on only one Chinese information retrieval course. More data and additional data sources could improve understanding of the MOOC forum phenomenon. Practical implications Since super degrees can reveal more latent information and identify high-quality threads and active participants, they can be used to assess how forum settings should be improved and to alleviate low forum participation. The proposed super degrees may also be applied in social network research. Originality/Value The paper provides definitions and algorithms for super degrees and applies them to forum analysis. Super degrees can help identify high-quality threads and active participants, supporting students in joining such threads and deepening their understanding of the knowledge MOOCs provide.
